To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the H. saimir-transformed tumor-reactve T cell lines provide an useful model of interactions of immune effector cells with AuTu and CD4+ T cell play a critical role of immune response to SCC of head and neck.
the virus-transformed CD4(+) T cells are capable of killing tumor cells and inducing expression of MHC molecules on tumor cells.
the virus-transformed CD4 T cells are more effective than the CD8 T cells in killing AuTu and in stimulating proliferation of CD8 T cells.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a novel immunotherapeutic strategy for the treatment of patients with head and neck cancer based on the use of tumor-reactive CD4+ and/or CD8+ T-cell lines.
the identification of T lymphocytes reactive against autologous tumor cells and the study of interactions between these tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes (TIL) and autologous tumor.
the development of novel approaches to the treatment of head and neck squamous cell carcinoma.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the H. saimiiri-transformed CD 8+ T cell lines were not able to kill the autologous tumor cells, while the H. saimirii-transformed CD4 + T cell lines could.

the H. saimiiri-transformed tumor reactive T cell lines are a useful model of interaction of immune effectors and AuTu, that CD4+ tumor reactive T cells play an important role in regulation of immune responses against squamous cell carcinoma, and that H. saimiir transformed tumor reactive CD4+ T cell lines can be a model for tumor immunotherapy.
H. saimiiri-transformed CD-4+ and CD-8+ T cells provide a useful model for the analysis of the interactions of immune effector cells with squamous cell carcinoma cells.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we are studying the interactions between autologous tumor cells and tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes.
we have shown that the CD4+ H. saimirii-transformed T cell line has the ability to recognize AuTu in a class II MHC-dependent manner.
we found that CD4+ cells are necessary to induce the expression of class I MHC antigens by AuTu.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we can take a patient's own tumor and grow a tumor-specific cytotoxic T cell (CTL) line.
CD8+ TCR Vbeta7+ T cells recognize AuTu in an MHC-restricted manner and are cytotoxic to AuTu, whereas CD4+ TCR V beta2+ T cells are cytotoxic to and proliferate upon contact with AuTu.
CD4+ and to a lesser extent CD8+ T-cells can be used to augment the immune response to head and neck cancer and to induce the expression of class I MHC antigens.
